newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche sees higher '97 net before provisons.
newsitem.headline: Roche sees higher '97 net before provisons.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG said it expected another good result for 1997 with an increase in group net profit before extraordinary provisions from acquisitions.
Roche also said in its six-month statement that it expected continued sales growth in the second half of 1997.
Roche's profit forecast is a repeat of the forecast it gave on July 15, when it released six-month sales figures.
"Barring unforeseen events, Roche anticipates a good overall result for 1997, with a further increase in consolidated net income before extraordinary provisions related to acquisitions," Roche said.
In 1996 Roche reported a 15.6 percent rise in its group net profit to 3.899 billion Swiss francs on sales of 15.966 billion.
On average analysts forecast Roche's 1997 group net profit to rise 7.2 percent to 4.18 billion francs.

However, the forecasts are attached with a great deal of uncertainty due to the planned acquisition of Bermunda-based Corange Ltd, the holding company for Germany's Boehringer Mannheim Group and U.S. based DePuy Inc..
The $11 billion acquisition, the largest in Roche's 100-year history, was announced in May. However, the deal has yet to be approved by authorities and thus be completed.

Roche has said the acquisition will dilute its earnings in the first year due to the cost of merging the two businesses and because the transaction will be financed by liquid funds, some of which yield high returns.
